commits.message:
Order replay findings against held events only when a re-execution is held

A replay union with no held member returns its findings without placing
them on the block's event order, so reconstructions that carry no
transition trace are classified as before.

Merge PR 471 head dabcc07640 into p1/t255

Eight conflicts, all in fault-proof test code. No validator or library
module needed a hand resolution.

The two forced-reason coordinate tests keep this branch's pin on the
terminal step's membership check of state.pre_utxos_root.

The input-existence chronology fixture and seed take PR 471's submitted
withdrawal rows, with the third seed deposit and the larger seed value
those rows need. They also keep this branch's deposit chronologies. The
same-block deposit now uses transaction-id byte 84. Byte 83 is now a seed
deposit, and the same-block deposit's output has to stay absent from the
predecessor ledger.

The lifecycle test now runs on PR 471's shared input-existence route
helper. The helper gains two options: a replacement step submitter, and a
refusal at step 03. The block-initial absence rows use both. The
withdrawal rows stay in PR 471's own submitted-withdrawal file.

The maximum-carriage test keeps this branch's deep ledger absence. It also
takes PR 471's explicit empty validation-trace header fields and its
own-output journal. The raw input-existence submitter keeps this branch's
claimed pre-root option.

UNMAPPED_VALIDATOR_COUNT is 526, which is the length of the merged list.
The registry test passes at 526 and fails at 525 and at 527.

The present-maximum journey now passes the own-output journal, which
field carriage publication now requires.

The rest merges automatically. It brings in the validation-trace dispute
runner and its one-step resolution, the case-on-constant CEK core arm,
script decoding split across six control-class stakers, and proof-thread
openers per source kind that reuse the opener's verified view. It also
brings input existence run on a submitted withdrawal and field carriage
identified by our own signed out-refs.

Drop the orphan funding cancel

The watcher no longer signs a cancel for orphaned funding. The cancel rows, the cancel wallet wiring and the cancel step of the orphan sweep are removed; the settle half of the sweep is unchanged.

Read the stage-four begin and stage-six fold-asset evidence by their own constructors

The script-sources middle yields read the auxiliary evidence by its
constructor. The stage-four begin yield now reads
TransactionRedeemerItemBeginWitness (27) and the stage-six fold-asset
yield reads MintFoldAssetWitness (35), the constructors the evidence type
gives these steps and the ones the off-chain writer emits. On-chain
vectors drive both yields through withdraw over an honest step, under
their own constructor and under another.

The runner now drives both steps like the other middle-yield roles: a
non-output step at stage four with the begin evidence, or at stage six
with the fold-asset evidence, carries its witness and role beside that
role's yield, and a stage-four begin step whose field is delivered by
reference waits. Each step has an emulator row through the award with
its refusals, replacing the rows that held them undriven.

Install the Plutus execution dispute in the public preprod catalogue

The owner put validationTraceDispute (00000006) in the preprod-public
catalogue at launch (2026-10-21). Drop it from the profile's exclusions and
from the curated emulator profile, which mirrors them. The nine families
with no installed off-chain workflow stay excluded, and mainnet keeps the
dispute excluded.

Shorten the public DA challenge window to 24 hours

Set da_challenge_window_ms to 86,400,000 on preprod-public and mainnet.
The withdrawal delay stays 778,080,000: block maturity still dominates
the challenge path (259,680,000 with the 48 h full response window).
The open-after-Apply margin (82,800,000 against a 2,160,000 floor), the
attestation ordering and the response budget still hold.

Regenerate the profiles and the Aiken environments, and move the public
figures in the profile tests, the DA bond literal tests, the deployments
README and decision 0002.
Weigh the new operator-watchdog test files in the node shard plan

Retry a failed watchdog takeover on a backoff and report it in readiness

A strike or forced retirement that failed for any reason other than a
script refusal ended the tick with a warning. The next tick retried on the
fiber's schedule, and after three failures citing the only undelivered
event the watchdog passed that event over and went idle, so the shift
stayed stalled.

A failed takeover now defers the watchdog on a doubling backoff from 10 s
up to 5 min and is retried until it lands. After three failures in a row
readiness reports operator_watchdog_takeover_failing with the last error. A
landed takeover, or a tick with no takeover due, clears it. An unfunded
wallet goes through the same backoff. A script refusal still passes over
its citation at once.

A citation passed over only because its attempts ran out is cited again
when no other event is citable. A refused citation is never cited again
under the same scheduler state.

Choose the strike's validity window when the strike is built

The watchdog planned a strike's validity window from the L1 time of the
tick, then ran the strike gate, the funding preflight and the reference
script and wallet reads before building it. A tick slower than the window
built a strike the ledger refused as expired.

The strike is now planned again from the same snapshot and citation, as of
the L1 time just before the build, so its window starts from that time. The
same planner chooses the bounds, so the on-chain checks on them still hold:
the range lies entirely after the inactivity threshold and the new shift
starts at its inclusive upper bound.

Pin the run's own unbuilt action appearing once in a named-state hold

A named-state run whose reason is also one of its alarms lists that
reason once in the readiness detail.

Alarm on a held validation-trace replay once its case open window is at risk

A header whose classification waits on a held script re-execution is now
logged at error level, with its readiness detail naming the end of the
case open window, once half the window or less is left or the header's
block time cannot be read. The threshold and window arithmetic are shared
with the held claim build alarm. The hold still decides nothing.
Weigh the new validation-trace test files in the fault-proofs shard plan
Merge the review fixes for the validation-trace install
